sections.content: How many people stayed in Brigg after gaining qualifications?

Brigg is a small town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Brigg does not have its own university.

Brigg has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Brigg ended up with:

  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 330 state-school pupils from Brigg who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 100 (30%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 105 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Brigg to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Brigg's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Brigg in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Of those in Brigg's GCSE cohort:

  • 35 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 37% of qualified non-graduates living in Brigg had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 95 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Brigg, compared with the 105 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 63% of qualified (level 3+) non-graduates in Brigg had also lived there when they sat their GCSEs, while 37% had moved there from elsewhere.
